title: Best online learning platforms for kids (2026): compared by type, age, and what your kid actually needs
summary: Compare Outschool, Khan Academy, IXL, Time4Learning, Connections Academy, and more by type, age, cost, and watch for
body_markdown:
## Virtual schools


### Connections Academy


**Best for:** families who want a full accredited public virtual school with state-certified teachers and IEP accommodation support


Connections Academy is a tuition-free public virtual school available in many states. Kids enroll as full-time learners, work with state-certified teachers, follow a structured curriculum, and receive a diploma. For families who want the credentials, legal protections, and IEP services of traditional school without the building, this is the model.


The trade-off is structure. There is a defined school calendar, required live attendance, standardized grading, and an assigned teacher. Many families describe it as public school at home. If you want curriculum freedom or your own pace, it often will not fit. For a fuller comparison of public virtual, private online, and homeschool, see[virtual school vs. homeschool](https://outschool.com/articles/virtual-school-vs-homeschool) .


- Tuition-free; accredited; state-certified teachers
- IEP accommodation services are legally required and provided
- Structured accountability; diploma upon graduation


**Watch for:** rigid schedule; required live attendance; limited flexibility; IEP service quality varies by state; not available in all states.


### K12 (Stride)


**Best for:** families who want a second virtual school option, often in states where Connections Academy is not offered


K12 operates virtual public schools under the Stride brand: accredited, tuition-free, state-certified teachers, and a diploma. The two programs operate in similar ways. K12 also has a private-tuition option (K12 Private Academy) for families who want the curriculum without enrolling in their state's public virtual school.


- Available in some states where Connections Academy is not
- Accredited; certified teachers; structured school calendar
- Private-tuition option if you want more control


**Watch for:** same structural limits as Connections Academy; more rigid than most homeschool setups; curriculum depth and teacher quality vary by state program.


## Tutoring


### Outschool 1-on-1 tutoring


**Best for:** targeted subject support, neurodiverse learners who need a tutor who gets how they learn, families who want to vet the tutor before committing


Outschool's 1-on-1 tutoring lets you search by subject, age group, teaching style, and experience with ADHD, dyslexia, giftedness, and other learning profiles. Every tutor has parent reviews on their profile. There is no upfront package, which matters when finding the right fit may take more than one try. Pair this with our[best online tutoring for kids](https://outschool.com/articles/best-online-tutoring-kids-comparison) comparison if you are weighing other tutoring brands.


- Search tutors by subject and specific experience
- Parent reviews on every tutor profile
- No upfront commitment; book single sessions


**Watch for:** tutor quality varies; finding the right fit may take a few sessions; availability can change.


### Varsity Tutors


**Best for:** test prep and structured subject support for older kids


Varsity Tutors offers live tutoring with session tools and test prep for SAT, ACT, and AP subjects. The content library and whiteboard tools are built for older kids preparing for high-stakes exams.


The platform often requires an upfront package before a family has had a single session. Families on public forums have described billing that is hard to exit and auto-renew packages. If you still need flexibility, that upfront commitment is a real risk.


- Strong test prep content for SAT, ACT, and AP
- Structured session tools and an interactive whiteboard


**Watch for:** upfront package before the first session; cancellation friction reported by families; a poor fit if you may need to switch tutors.


## Learning games


### Prodigy


**Best for:** early elementary math engagement, a motivational entry point for kids who resist every other practice format


Prodigy is a fantasy game in which kids advance by answering math questions. It covers first through eighth grade and the basic version is free. For younger kids who will play a game but will not sit with a worksheet, it solves the motivation problem. It is a supplement, not a program. The game mechanic can encourage fast guessing, and it often loses steam in middle school.


- Free basic version; game format for younger kids
- Covers first through eighth grade; parent dashboard shows topics


**Watch for:** fast-guessing; no live instruction; supplement only; weaker past elementary for many kids.


### Duolingo


**Best for:** a daily language habit, vocabulary exposure, a free entry point into a second language


Duolingo's gamified structure works well for building a daily language habit. The app is free and effective at introducing vocabulary and basic sentence patterns. It does not produce conversational fluency or teach grammar in a systematic way. Use it as a daily warm-up next to a live language class, not as the whole program.


- Free; engaging format for young learners
- Good for daily vocabulary and a language habit


**Watch for:** limited fluency; weak grammar instruction; no live conversation.


### Epic!


**Best for:** building a reading habit, independent reading across genres and levels


Epic! is a digital library of 40,000+ books, audiobooks, and learning videos for kids ages 12 and under. It removes the friction of sourcing books. It is not a reading instruction tool and does not teach phonics or comprehension strategies.


- Large library across levels and genres
- Easy for kids to browse on most devices


**Watch for:** not a reading instruction program; no live component; limited free tier; age cap at 12.


## How to choose the right platform


- **Your kid has stopped using apps and self-paced tools.** That is often the signal they need a live teacher, not a better app. Outschool is the next step for many families.
- **You need a free academic supplement for a motivated learner.** Khan Academy covers K-12 at no cost.
- **You want school-aligned tracking.** IXL gives the most granular standards data, with the caveat that it is a poor fit for anxious or struggling learners.
- **You need full curriculum coverage.** Time4Learning is the most structured turn-key option on this list.
- **You want a fully accredited school experience.** Connections Academy or K12 deliver that at no tuition cost where they operate.
- **Your kid is young and needs an engaging entry point.** ABCmouse, Prodigy, or Epic! are low-friction starting points. Pair with live classes when they are ready for more.
- **Your kid needs targeted 1-on-1 support.** Search Outschool tutors by subject and learning profile, and read what other families say before you book.


Browse[live online classes on Outschool](https://outschool.com/online-classes) across academics, enrichment, and 1-on-1 tutoring.


## FAQ


### What is the best online learning platform for kids?


It depends on the job. Live small-group classes and 1-on-1 tutoring fit kids who stall on apps. Self-paced tools like Khan Academy and IXL fit motivated independent practice. Virtual schools fit families who want an accredited diploma. Games fit younger kids as a supplement.


### Can I use ESA funds for online learning platforms?


In many states, live classes, tutoring, and some online programs are approved expenses. Rules vary by program. Start with[what is an education savings account](https://outschool.com/esa-guides/what-is-education-savings-account) and the[ESA approved expenses list](https://outschool.com/esa-guides/approved-list) before you book.


### Is a subscription better than pay-per-class?


A subscription is cheaper if your kid logs in every week. Pay-per-class is cheaper if they stall after two weeks, which is a common pattern on self-paced tools. Watch the first 14 days before you lock in a year.
